members.reason: [llm] duplicates #1784: Both address stored/restored OAuth tokens forcing a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. #1784 fixes the root cause in _initialize(): token_expiry_time is never computed when tokens are loaded from storage, so is_token_valid() can't detect expiry. #2875's own inline comment cites this exact same root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') and works around it by adding a new refresh-token attempt inside async_auth_flow's 403 handling before falling back to full re-authorization.

members.title: Fix: Raise RuntimeError when ClientSession is used without context manager to prevent hangs
members.author: newbiehwang
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2631: ClientSession's async context-manager lifecycle isn't validated: using it without ever entering (`async with`), or entering it twice, currently leads to silent hangs/undefined behavior instead of a clear error. Both PRs converge on the exact same fix mechanism — a new `_entered` boolean attribute on ClientSession, declared/initialized in the same spot in __init__ and checked in __aenter__ — so they touch the same lines and would conflict directly on merge.

clusters.pick_reason: #2654 targets the current codebase (uses the `create_context_streams` wrapper already present at HEAD) and ships a reproducing regression test (`BlockingStdout`) that exercises the exact notification-then-response blocking scenario, fixing it by default with buffer size 1. #2215's diff is against the pre-refactor code (calls `anyio.create_memory_object_stream` directly rather than `create_context_streams`), so it predates the `_context_streams` refactor the other three PRs are built on and would need a rebase/likely hits a merge conflict on the same lines. members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both rewrite `RequestResponder.cancel()` in src/mcp/shared/session.py to stop the responder from sending an (erroneous) JSON-RPC response/error for a request that has been cancelled, per MCP/JSON-RPC spec ('receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request'). clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the identical two except-blocks in auth/utils.py (lines ~243 and ~334-336) plus session.py, so they conflict on the same lines and only one can land cleanly. #2565 is the minimal, additive fix: it only appends `from e` and leaves the original f-string message (`f"Invalid registration response: {e}"`) untouched. #2777 goes further and also rewrites the message text to a static string, dropping the interpolated exception detail from the message itself (relying solely on the chained traceback to surface it) — a behavior change beyond the stated scope of 'add raise ... from e'. Keeping the smaller, message-preserving diff (#2565) avoids that incidental message-text change while still fixing the exception-chaining bug; #2777's version can be closed as a duplicate of the same underlying gap.
